findings.evidence: Asymptotics.lean:125-129 contains the whole argument locally; Cocompact.lean:19-27 advertises the module as the home of the `x⁻¹`-decay estimates and exports only the `IsBigO` direction (`isBigO_inv_mul_inv_sq`, Cocompact.lean:76-78).
findings.fix: Add a public `Asymptotics.isLittleO_inv_sq_inv_cocompact : (fun x : 𝕜 => (x ^ 2)⁻¹) =o[cocompact 𝕜] fun x => x⁻¹` (with `[ProperSpace 𝕜]`) to `Mathematics/Analysis/Asymptotics/Cocompact.lean`, list it in that module's docstring bullet list, and prove the `isLittleO` theorem as `(isBigO_... ).trans_isLittleO isLittleO_inv_sq_inv_cocompact`.
findings.issue: `(fun x : ℝ => x⁻¹) =o[cocompact ℝ] (1 : ℝ)` and the resulting `(x ^ 2)⁻¹ =o[cocompact 𝕜] x⁻¹` are proved as an inline `have`/`refine` inside `isLittleO_sphericalBesselJ_sub_sin_div_inv_cocompact`. This is general infrastructure (upstream types only, nothing Bessel-specific) and is the `o`-counterpart of the exported `Asymptotics.isBigO_inv_mul_inv_sq`; any consumer converting another `O(1 / x ^ 2)` result in this file to the roadmap's `o(1 / x)` vocabulary must re-prove it.

findings.evidence: Asymptotics.lean:97-147: `j_l` gets `isBigO_sphericalBesselJ_inv_cocompact`, `tendsto_sphericalBesselJ_cocompact`, the `O(1/x^2)` and the `o(1/x)` forms; `deriv (sphericalBesselJ l)` gets only `isBigO_deriv_sphericalBesselJ_sub_cos_div_inv_sq_cocompact`. Roadmap LightNuclei/README.md:374-377 states the asymptotics bullet in the `o(1/x)` vocabulary; Cocompact.lean:84-87 exports only the `sin` bound.
findings.fix: Export `isLittleO_deriv_sphericalBesselJ_sub_cos_div_inv_cocompact` and `isBigO_deriv_sphericalBesselJ_inv_cocompact` (one line each given the lemma of the previous finding), and add the `cos` companion `Real.isBigO_cos_comp_one` to `Cocompact.lean` that the decay form needs, next to `isBigO_sin_comp_one`.
findings.issue: The `j_l` side is exported in four parallel forms (`isBigO_..._sub_sin_inv`, `isBigO_..._sub_sin_div_inv_sq`, `isLittleO_..._sub_sin_div_inv`, `isBigO_sphericalBesselJ_inv` + `tendsto_...`), but the derivative side only in the `O(1 / x ^ 2)` form, including no form in the `o(1 / x)` vocabulary the roadmap names as canonical and no `deriv j_l = O(1 / x)` decay statement — so §0.4/§5.3 consumers of the derivative asymptotics have to redo the conversions.

summary: The exported surface is otherwise clean (no compatibility artifacts, nothing wrongly private, docstring listings accurate), but the general `o`-conversion step is buried in a proof body instead of exported from the new `Cocompact` module that exists to hold exactly such facts, and the derivative asymptotics is exported only in the `O(1 / x ^ 2)` form while `j_l` gets four parallel forms.
